name: Brown Olive
lede: Brown Olive is a very dark, almost black olive-brown; as a name it echoes the old naturalists' olive brown, and as a color it is the dark ground of a great many paintings.

sections.title: Olive and brown together
sections.body: Brown Olive is a descriptive pairing of two basic color words, not a traditional name [1]. The older compound in the books runs the other way round: *olive brown* is listed in the nomenclature of colors that Syme prepared from Werner's mineral scheme, and it recurs in the index of Baty's study of that system [1][2]. The same list names an olive or clove brown among its browns [2]. Compare the greener [[olive-green]] and the yellower [[khaki]].

sections.title: Dye shades
sections.body: The Pigment Compendium notes that the extract catechu dyes cloth a fast color that varies between brown, olive and khaki [3]. Catechu is a tannin-rich extract from a southern Asian tree [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This is one of the commonest colors in the ColorHub archive: 5,787 of 23,781 paintings, about 24 percent, contain it within our match threshold, as photographed [4]. In the lightness order of those paintings it is a shadow color about 71 percent of the time and a midtone about 28 percent [4]. The painter who relies on it most in our data is Erik Pauelsen, with 12 of his 15 paintings, and Johan Heinrich Neuman has it in 10 of 12 [4]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so the dark olive is partly the varnish [4].
